title: Don't cloneDeep a DataFrame you only read from
answers: Why was cloneDeep removed from RawListContainer?
Should I clone a DataFrame prop before reading its fields?
Avoiding unnecessary deep clones of DataFrame in React components
body:
Fix pattern: RawListContainer used cloneDeep(tableResult) on a DataFrame prop even though it never mutated the frame, just read fields/values from it; removing the clone and using the prop directly avoids needless copying and the strict-mode cloneDeep crash risk from getter-only derived fields on frame implementations.
Constraints: applies when a component only reads from a DataFrame (fields, values, length) — if a component genuinely mutates the frame it still needs its own copy, but prefer a shallow/structural copy over cloneDeep on frame objects that expose derived getters.
applies: React components/hooks in public/app that receive DataFrame props and only read (don't mutate) them.
says: Why was cloneDeep removed from RawListContainer?
Should I clone a DataFrame prop before reading its fields?
Avoiding unnecessary deep clones of DataFrame in React components
search: Avoid cloneDeep on DataFrame props that components only read from, not mutate. Unnecessary cloning causes performance waste and triggers strict-mode crashes on getter-only derived fields. The rule applies to React components and hooks in public/app that receive DataFrame props and access their fields, values, or length without mutation; use the prop directly instead. If a component genuinely mutates the frame, prefer shallow or structural copies over cloneDeep. Affects RawListContainer in public/app/features/explore/PrometheusListView/.
